narrative.overview: One paper sheet carries the evidence; the machine side (header, incident strip, decision rail, a slim frame) sits on a deep indigo ground. The sheet is the only lit surface and holds the only shadow. Inside it, structure is lines, not boxes. The recruiter reads one incident top to bottom (caught, priced, contract, decision), then approves in the rail.
keyCharacteristics: Paper dominates; indigo is header, strip, rail and a slim frame (`--frame` 1.5rem).
One shadow in the whole UI (the sheet). Everything inside is hairlines.
Money is the loudest type: marigold on the indigo, tabular figures, Indian grouping (Rs 1,73,622).
Honest machine: elapsed times and step counts are shown as recorded, never faked.

rules.name: The Red Is a Clock Rule
rules.body: Red appears only for a running deadline: the rail countdown, the strip's clock icon, the phone bar subline. When the clock closes it goes muted; it never marks errors or emphasis.

rules.name: The Marigold Money Rule
rules.body: On the indigo, marigold is money at risk and nothing else; it turns mint when the money is saved. On paper the same roles use the darker Amber and Mint.

rules.name: The Two Sets Rule
rules.body: Components read the ink and line tokens instead of hard-coding colours, so they work on both the indigo and the paper.

rules.name: The Text Floor Rule
rules.body: No text under --t1: 15 px at 1440 and above (it scales up), 14 px on phones.

rules.name: The Tabular Rupee Rule
rules.body: Every rupee figure, time, count and duration uses tabular, lining numerals. Rupees use Indian grouping and a non-breaking space after Rs.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only the sheet casts a shadow. Inside the sheet, depth is a hairline plus the slip tone.

dos: Do write every size in rem so the composition scales with the viewport.
Do keep text at or above `--t1`.
Do use red only for a running deadline, and marigold (on the indigo) only for money at risk.
Do show the agent's real step counts and milliseconds, and state why a control is disabled.
Do show a fix's result as before and after in the rail preview.
Do keep one shadow (the sheet); use hairlines and the slip tone inside it.
Do use the token variables for text and lines so a component works on both indigo and paper.
donts: Don't add a second shadow, a box around the rail, or a full-bleed map console.
Don't use red for errors; errors are an ink note with an edge border.
Don't shrink text below the floor to fit; reflow instead.
Don't size geometry from raw viewport maths; anchor to content and rem.
Don't request external fonts or scripts at runtime.
Don't fake streaming or hide latency, fallbacks or role limits.
